clue.text: Put in amount that's to be coughed up

definitions.note: a noun phrase: something brought up by coughing

indicators.note: the word put is placed inside a word for amount, so in signals the container

parts.note: a sum is an amount, as of money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told to add a sum to a payment that must be handed over reluctantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coughed up' reads as paying unwillingly; here it is literal, phlegm brought up from the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputum is the mucus and saliva brought up from the lungs by coughing.

clue.text: Sausage Evita got in burst pipe

indicators.note: Evita gets inside the scrambled pipe, so got in marks the container
a burst pipe is broken open, so its letters are scattered

parts.note: Eva Peron, wife of the Argentine president, was known as Evita

explanation.surface: An Argentine first lady stuck in a broken water pipe with a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burst' shuffles the pipe's letters to PEPI; 'got in' then sets Evita's surname inside that run, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy dried Italian-American salami often used on pizza.

clue.text: Global hotline?

parts.note: a line drawn on the globe that bounds the hot zone near the equator

explanation.definitionFit: Cancer and Capricorn are parallels of latitude enclosing the world's hottest band.

clue.text: The domestic, non-CE, might be this

definitions.text: The domestic, non-CE, might be this

indicators.note: might be this suggests the remaining letters could turn into something else
non tells us the letters C and E are left out

parts.note: the Church of England, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A household servant who isn't Anglican could belong to another church.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop C and E from THE DOMESTIC to leave nine letters and rearrange them; a Methodist is indeed outside the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodists are a Protestant denomination that broke away from the Church of England.

clue.text: Vegetable in general is sticky stuff

indicators.note: the sticky stuff sits within the general's name, so in marks the container

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general, is the crossword's stock general
gum is a sticky substance

explanation.surface: A claim that, generally speaking, a vegetable is a gluey substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' looks like the phrase meaning usually; it splits into the container signal 'in' and General Lee.
explanation.definitionFit: A legume is a pod vegetable such as a pea, bean or lentil.

clue.text: Deposit English gold pieces

indicators.note: pieces suggests the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Banking English gold coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' reads as coins; it is the signal to break up E and GOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to deposit, as in lodging money or a document with someone.

clue.text: Scientific study gets nice muddle

indicators.note: a muddle is a jumble, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A field of research becomes a pleasant mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetics is the branch of biology studying heredity and genes.

clue.text: To a degree mother can be deadly

definitions.note: a phrase describing the snake, which can kill

indicators.note: to means attached to, so the mother is joined onto the degree

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: To some extent, a mother can be lethal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a degree' looks like the phrase meaning somewhat; it supplies the joining signal and MBA.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a highly venomous African snake whose bite can kill.

clue.text: Being cross in polite fashion is an achievement

indicators.note: the cross mark is set inside the rearranged word, so in signals the container
to fashion is to shape or make anew, so the letters of polite are reshaped

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Managing to be angry while staying courteous counts as a real accomplishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry but gives the letter X, which goes into EPLOIT, the letters of 'polite' reshaped by 'fashion'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a daring or notable deed, a feat worth recording.

clue.text: Ineligible for joining the green party?

definitions.text: Ineligible for joining the green party?

parts.words: Ineligible for joining the green party?
parts.note: green means new to something, so a seasoned veteran would not belong to a gathering of novices

explanation.definitionFit: Being skilled through practice is the opposite of being green or new to something.

clue.text: In police department a lot are backward, if forceful …

indicators.note: backward tells us the whole assembled run is read from its end to its start
a lot is placed inside the police department, so In marks the container

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
many means a lot of

explanation.surface: A remark that many in a police unit lag behind, even if they are energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The container makes CIMANYD, and 'backward' turns that whole run round; 'if' and 'are' are only links, with the ellipsis tying the clue to the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic describes someone vigorous and energetic, full of driving force.

clue.text: Cut glass collections that once ruled the waves?

parts.note: crystal is fine cut glass
sets are collections of things

explanation.surface: Fine glassware sets that once dominated the seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruled the waves' evokes Britannia's navy; the waves are radio waves, which early crystal radio receivers picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Early radio receivers using a crystal detector dominated broadcast listening before valve sets.

clue.text: … with full authority half of police are deployed in jail

indicators.note: deployed means spread out and placed strategically, so the three letters are scattered through the jail word
half of takes the first three of the six letters of police

parts.note: a penitentiary is a prison, especially in the US

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: officers with full powers being sent into a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters from 'police' do not stay together: 'deployed' scatters them, one after the jail word's first letter and two later, so the parse shows a mix of both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenipotentiary is an envoy invested with full power to act for a government.

clue.text: Crossover door

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word door is flipped end to end

explanation.surface: A door that changes sides, like a crossover in a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossover' looks like one word; split it into the definition 'Cross' and the reversal signal 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially the large cross over a church's chancel screen.

clue.text: Choice of boats — but for the spelling!

indicators.note: but for the spelling says the phrase is identical when heard, differing only on paper

parts.note: which craft? is the question when choosing between boats

explanation.surface: Picking a boat, where only the written form tells two phrases apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelling' does double duty in the joke: it is the definition (casting spells) and the surface says the two phrases differ only in how they are written.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting spells is the practice of magic, so spelling here means sorcery.

clue.text: Where trim ankle maybe sets one back a lot?

definitions.text: Where trim ankle maybe sets one back a lot?

parts.note: to clip is to trim
an ankle is an example of a joint

explanation.surface: A place where a shapely ankle proves expensive to the visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets one back a lot' means costs a great deal, the hallmark of a venue that overcharges.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip joint is a nightclub or bar that overcharges or swindles customers.

clue.text: Boeing aircraft once based down under?

definitions.text: Boeing aircraft once based down under?

parts.words: Boeing aircraft once based down under?
parts.note: posing as a plane once stationed in Australia, the letters of Boeing and air mix to describe an original Australian

explanation.walkthrough: Within 'aircraft', 'craft' works as a shuffle signal on BOEING and AIR; since a word cannot be split here, the clue is shown whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboriginal Australians are the continent's first inhabitants, there long before European settlement.

clue.text: Awful fuss with bill ends up happy

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, so these letters are put in bad order

explanation.surface: After a dreadful row over the bill, things end on a cheerful note.
explanation.definitionFit: Blissful means full of great joy, extremely happy.

clue.text: Piglet, so it might appear, stops food going the wrong way

definitions.text: stops food going the wrong way
definitions.note: a verb phrase describing what the flap does, standing for the noun

indicators.note: might appear says these letters could show up in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh's friend Piglet is seen, apparently, preventing choking.
explanation.definitionFit: This flap of cartilage closes over the windpipe during swallowing, keeping food out of the airway.

clue.text: Get in a twist about fuel?

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Becoming flustered over the price of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get in a twist' sounds like getting upset; read literally it is winding into loops.
explanation.definitionFit: To coil is to wind into rings or spirals, twisting round on itself.

clue.text: It's very large to attack

parts.note: assai is the Italian musical term for very, as in allegro assai
L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Something enormous enough to go on the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSAI is a musical direction meaning very, worth knowing from scores.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, physically or with words.

clue.text: Part of meal is mere cold sweet, something liable to perversion

parts.note: a course of a meal is one part of it, such as the main
just means merely, nothing more than
an ice is a frozen dessert

explanation.surface: A diner remarks that one dish is only a chilled pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the offence of perverting the course of justice, obstructing the legal process.
explanation.definitionFit: English law names the offence of perverting legal process, so this phrase is what gets perverted.

clue.text: Single leading lady kept in the dark

indicators.note: the lady's initial is held within the single, so kept marks the container

parts.note: a unit is a single thing

indicators.note: leading picks the first letter of lady

explanation.surface: An unmarried leading actress kept uninformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' reads as a star actress; it gives just L, put inside UNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means without light, so anything unlit is left in darkness.

clue.text: Rejected overture, if not drunk

indicators.note: if not tells us the letters of if are removed
rejected means thrown back, so the overture's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Fidelio, Beethoven's only opera, has a well-known overture

explanation.surface: An opening offer turned down, as if one weren't sober.
explanation.walkthrough: FIDELIO reversed is OILEDIF; 'not' then removes IF. 'Overture' looks like an offer, but it is the opera's.
explanation.definitionFit: Well oiled is slang for drunk, so oiled alone means tipsy.

clue.text: Attitude of one on benefit?

parts.note: the dole is British state unemployment benefit, so someone on it might be said to be full of it

explanation.definitionFit: Doleful means sorrowful and gloomy, the mood one might expect of someone out of work.

clue.text: Aussie town detailed in its leaning uprights

indicators.note: the shortened town is set within the word its, so in marks the container

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: detailed means with its tail cut off, losing the final letter

parts.note: Alice Springs, the Northern Territory town, is known simply as Alice

explanation.surface: An Australian town described in close detail, with its upright posts tilting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like thorough; read as de-tailed it removes the last letter of ALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, so its letters are slanted versions of upright characters.

clue.text: It's old — oddly unemotional

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something aged, which strangely shows no feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive, calm and showing little emotion.

clue.text: German dramatist — rings a bell?

definitions.meaning: Ernst ... was a German expressionist playwright of the 1920s
one who tolls is someone who rings a bell slowly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings a bell' suggests the name is familiar; it is a literal description of a bell-ringer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernst Toller wrote expressionist plays, and a bell-tolling person is also so called.
